title: Interleaved JSON + Tool Protocol: PRD and Acceptance Criteria for Streaming Function Handoffs
creator: Maya Chen
description: This PRD defines the acceptance criteria and testable behavior for streaming responses that interleave structured JSON fragments with tool/function invocation events. It covers how the platform should emit, validate, and recover from malformed or partial JSON chunks, how function calls are declared and resolved mid-stream, and the observable contract SDKs expose to integrators.
goal: Ship a backwards-compatible streaming output contract that allows models to interleave JSON payloads and function/tool call events without increasing client parsing complexity, while providing deterministic error modes and clear fallback behavior for runtime and tooling teams.
scope_included: Streaming protocol event types for: json_chunk, json_close, tool_call_start, tool_call_end, tool_error, text_chunk
Schema validation rules for JSON fragments and final composite objects
Clear contract for function/tool invocation metadata: idempotency token, proposed args, target tool id, version
Retry and fallback semantics when encountering invalid JSON or tool failures
SDK parsing helpers and example usage in JS/Python to reassemble interleaved streams into coherent JSON+tool call records
Telemetry events and logs required for debugging streaming contract failures
scope_excluded: Changes to model prompting strategies or model-side code generation heuristics
Non-streaming batch APIs (text generation API behavior remains unchanged)
Tool implementation details (how external tools execute business logic)
acceptance_criteria: A. Event envelope: Every streaming frame must include an event_type header with one of: json_chunk, json_close, tool_call_start, tool_call_end, tool_error, text_chunk. SDKs must expose an iterator that yields parsed events in order.

B. JSON reassembly: Clients using SDK helpers must be able to reassemble interleaved json_chunk frames into the original JSON object; broken or missing json_close must surface a deterministic error with code STREAM_JSON_INCOMPLETE.

C. Partial-object validation: The runtime will validate each completed JSON object against the supplied schema (when provided) and emit a schema_violation event if the final object fails validation. Schema violations must not cause the stream to terminate by default; they should be emitted as tool_error with severity 'validation' and included in the final completion metadata.

D. Tool invocation handshake: A tool_call_start frame must include call_id, tool_id, args_preview (partial or full), and idempotency_token. The platform must guarantee at-most-once delivery for tool_call_start by honoring idempotency_token on retries across the same completion request.

E. Mid-stream tool resolution: tool_call_end frames contain call_id, status (ok|failed|skipped), result_ref (if ok), and optional diagnostic message. The ordering of tool_call_end relative to subsequent json_chunk frames must be preserved by the stream consumer.

1) If a malformed JSON chunk is received and cannot be reassembled, emit STREAM_JSON_MALFORMED and include byte_offset and last_good_seq in diagnostics. Default behavior: continue streaming text_chunk fallback unless client opted-in to strict_mode.
2) If a tool_call_start is sent but the tool fails to initialize, emit tool_error with error_type 'init' and include suggested fallback: 'text_fallback' or 'no-op'.

G. Backwards compatibility: Non-upgraded SDKs should still receive text_chunk frames that contain a readable textual fallback if structured events are not supported by the client or when strict failures occur.

H. Observability: The runtime must emit telemetry for each stream containing stream_id, total_events, first_schema_violation_timestamp (if any), tool_calls_count, and final_stream_status to the Console events pipeline within 5s of stream completion.
I. Performance: End-to-end added latency for emitting events and reassembly helpers should not increase median completion latency by more than 5% on standard benchmarks used by runtime team.

J. Docs & SDKs: JS and Python SDKs must include examples for three flows: successful interleaved JSON + tool calls, JSON malformed then fallback, and tool fails then retry-idempotency behavior. Each example must include parsing snippets and recommended error handling.

K. Security: All tool invocation metadata must be redacted from public logs; only hashed tool_id and truncated call_id may appear in ingest telemetry. Security review sign-off required before release.
test_scenarios: 1) Happy path: stream emits json_chunk*, json_close, tool_call_start, tool_call_end(ok) and final metadata: client SDK reassembles objects, validates schema, associates tool result by call_id.

2) Malformed json_chunk in the middle: runtime emits STREAM_JSON_MALFORMED diagnostic; SDK switches to text_chunk fallback and returns a partial object error to application with suggested remediation.
3) Missing json_close: after stream ends without json_close frame, SDK raises STREAM_JSON_INCOMPLETE and includes last_good_seq; runtime produces a postmortem telemetry event.
4) Tool init failure: tool_call_start followed by tool_error(init); client receives fallback text_chunk; platform records tool_error with diagnostic and suggested retry window.
5) Duplicate tool_call_start with same idempotency_token: platform deduplicates and returns the same tool result reference without re-executing tool.
6) High-throughput: interleaved event stream with 50 tool calls and 200 JSON fragments under 1s; ensure observability event emitted and median latency within SLA.

7) Schema violation after reassembly: runtime emits schema_violation event but stream remains; SDK surfaces validation error in final metadata and includes raw payload for debugging (redacted per policy).
rollout_notes: Phase 1 (Canary): Enable interleaved streaming for 5% of hosted traffic with SDKs opted-in via feature flag; capture telemetry and errors to a dedicated dashboard.
Phase 2 (Gradual): Expand to 50% while instrumenting supportability SLOs and raising alerts for STREAM_JSON_MALFORMED > 0.5% of sessions.
Phase 3 (GA): Default-on for new model versions after 2 weeks of stable telemetry. Provide migration guide for customers relying on text-only fallbacks.
Rollback criteria: increase in client-side parsing errors by >3x, or tool invocation at-most-once violations observed in production.
open_questions: Q1: Should strict_mode be opt-in at the completion request level or at the account level? Recommendation: request-level opt-in to avoid breaking existing customers.
Q2: Do we allow nested tool_calls (tool invokes another tool) in the same stream? Recommendation: disallow nested tool invocations in v1; support in future if demand appears.
Q3: What is the canonical format for args_preview when arguments are too large? Recommendation: truncated base64 or hash with redaction policy.
Q4: How to surface partial-object warnings to end-customers without exposing PII? Use redaction and include only structural diffs in telemetry.
decisions: D1: Use event envelope with event_type header instead of ad-hoc tokens in text to make SDK parsing deterministic.
D2: Default behavior on JSON reassembly failures is to continue with text_chunk fallback unless strict_mode=true.
D3: Enforce idempotency_token deduplication for tool_call_start to provide at-most-once semantics for customer tools.
D4: All public docs must include example error-handling patterns and sample telemetry queries for debugging.
definition_of_done: PRD reviewed and approved by Runtime, SDK, Security, and Console PMs.
Runtime implementation merged and feature-flagged in staging with unit+integration tests.
JS/Python SDK helpers implemented and published as beta packages with examples.
Console dashboard for streaming protocol telemetry created and alerts configured.
Security review completed and redaction rules enforced in telemetry pipeline.
Customer migration guide published and included in release notes.
notes: This ticket combines learnings from prior ad-hoc streaming experiments; aim is to reduce parsing ambiguity customers face when models emit JSON and tool events together.
Coordination required with Console for telemetry ingestion schema changes and with Support to prepare triage playbook for stream-related incidents.
Estimate assumes ENG will deliver core runtime hooks and SDK team will implement reassembly helpers concurrently.
